Hillside Primary School
Be the BEST you can be
Hillside Primary School
Robinswood Primary Academy has been renamed Hillside Primary School, following the amalgamation with Moat Primary Academy.
The new name represents a fresh start for our united school community and reflects the new identity we are building together. The renaming is a significant milestone on this journey, one that celebrates the strengths of both schools while looking confidently to the future.
At Hillside, we have high expectations, and the needs of our pupils are at the heart of all we do. Our aim is to provide a caring and safe environment for our children to become confident, caring, resilient and curious; we encourage them to achieve the very best that they can across every area of school curriculum.
Hillside Primary School is a proud member of the Greenshaw Learning Trust, a ‘family’ of like-minded schools, that collaborate to provide mutual support, share their good practice and learn from each other, whilst retaining and developing their own distinctive character. You can read more about the Greenshaw Learning Trust here.
Rebekah Millward, Headteacher

About Us
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Hillside Primary School where we aim for our children to 'be the best that they can be’.
Welcome to Hillside Primary School, where everyone is immensely proud to be part of a kind, honest, respectful and responsible team. We all work together to be the BEST we can be, every day in everything we do.
We are a large primary school with our own preschool on site and a range of facilities including a large field, a sports hall and an inspiring forest school. I am very proud to be the Headteacher and work hard with our dedicated team of staff to make a difference for all our children. Our pastoral and SEND support is strong, and we are passionate about insuring every child’s needs are met.
The local community and our parents are vital to our work in school, and we take pride in being involved in numerous events and opening our doors to all the friends of Hillside, parents and carers.
Our curriculum is engaging and aspirational, preparing our children for a bright and successful future in whatever they desire to do. All children are expected to learn how to build strong relationships and to understand that working together to put things right makes us kind, honest, respectful and responsible people.
Please come and visit us at Hillside, where everyone is always welcome.
Rebekah Millward, Headteacher

Learning Curriculum
Learning Curriculum
Our Subjects
Religious Education
Religious Education
At Hillside Primary School, our Religious Education (RE) curriculum is designed to place the needs, identities, and aspirations of our pupils at the heart of their learning. Our bespoke curriculum is ambitious and inclusive, empowering every child to think like a theologian, philosopher, and social scientist, fostering a deep respect for the diverse beliefs that shape our world to help them "Be the BEST they can be."
Our RE curriculum intent is underpinned by our four key attitudes for learning, ensuring pupils develop the empathy and critical thinking needed to thrive in a multi-faith and non-religious modern world:
We deliver a high-quality RE curriculum—rooted in the Jigsaw RE enquiry-based model—that equips pupils with Substantive Knowledge (religious facts, texts, and traditions) and Disciplinary Knowledge (the ability to analyse, interpret, and evaluate). Our curriculum is anchored by six ‘Big Ideas’ that build progressively, helping pupils construct a mental schema of how faith and worldviews influence human experience.
BELIEVE: Building Confidence and Belonging
Identity & Belonging (Big Idea): We foster an environment where children believe in the value of their own voice. By exploring Jigsaw RE’s focus on 'The Personal', children first understand their own 'insider' perspective before looking at the wider world.
Vocabulary for Success: We believe vocabulary is the gateway to understanding complex worldviews. Pupils progress from simple terms like 'Faith' and 'Kindness' in EYFS to mastering tier-3 terminology such as ‘Covenant’, ‘Secularism’, ‘Dharma’, and ‘Atheism’.
Inclusive Achievement: Through the Jigsaw RE approach, we ensure all pupils – regardless of faith background or SEND needs – believe they can access the 'Big Questions' of life through scaffolded discussion and sensory learning.
ENGAGE: Curiosity and Connection
Practices & Lifestyles (Big Idea): We spark curiosity by investigating how beliefs are lived out in the real world, from the rituals of Salah to the celebration of Diwali.
Theological Enquiry (Disciplinary): Following the Jigsaw RE 4-step process (Engagement, Investigation, Evaluation, Expression), pupils engage as active investigators. They move from asking 'Why is this object special?' in KS1 to 'How do religious texts influence modern ethics?' in KS2.
Local Identity: We connect our learning to the local community. By visiting local places of worship in Gloucester—from the Cathedral to local Mosques and Gurdwaras—children see faith as a living part of their own city's story.
SUCCEED: Precision & Mastery
Beliefs & Teachings (Big Idea): Success is rooted in an accurate understanding of core tenets. Pupils move from knowing religious stories to mastering the complex theology behind them, such as the Five Pillars of Islam or the concept of Salvation in Christianity.
Interpretation (Disciplinary): Mastery is shown when pupils can explain why people within the same religion might disagree or practice differently, demonstrating an understanding of diversity within faith.
Substantive Mastery: Pupils succeed when they can compare worldviews with precision, such as contrasting the concept of God in monotheistic faiths with dharmic traditions or humanistic perspectives.
TRY: Resilience & Hard Thinking
Ethics & Values (Big Idea): Pupils embrace 'hard thinking' to tackle complex moral dilemmas. They 'try' out different philosophical stances to understand concepts of justice, peace, and the environment.
Critical Reflection (Disciplinary): We cultivate a culture where children are not afraid to challenge ideas and be challenged. They learn that 'trying' to understand a perspective different from their own is the first step toward social cohesion.
Meaning & Purpose (Big Idea): Children develop resilience by grappling with the 'Big Questions' of existence, such as 'Why do people suffer?' or 'What happens when we die?', understanding that different worldviews offer different answers.

About Us
safeguarding curriculum
safeguarding curriculum
Pupil safeguarding is of primary importance at Hillside Primary School. The school is committed to supporting and educating children across a range of safeguarding matters, as well as supporting issues specifically related to our local context.
We seek opportunities in the taught curriculum for children to learn about safeguarding. Our PSHE curriculum covers safeguarding themes through each of the strands within the Jigsaw scheme of work. We are sensitive in our teaching and recognise that some more sensitive subjects need to be taught at an age-appropriate level, or within a small group or 1:1 level where a more urgent need arises. We teach Relationships and Sex education and support pupils in understanding the importance of learning about healthy relationships. We teach online safety in each year group but also respond to any issues that arise through further lessons, assemblies or by using external agencies, i.e - the community police/PCSOs.
Building resilience
Children are taught about how to make the right choices to keep themselves safe. We refer to safeguarding practices in school regularly, such as which coloured lanyards visitors wear and mobile phone and internet safety through our assemblies and curriculum (as examples).
We talk to pupils about having trusted adults in school who they can go to if they have worries. Children are regularly reminded to talk to staff if they do not feel safe and happy. At the start of each term, children complete an activity: "I wish my adults knew..." This allows the children to let staff know what is important to them and if they have any worries or concerns. The children have access to this box every day.

Early reading and Phonics​​​​​​​
Early reading and Phonics​​​​​​​
Early reading and phonics
At Hillside Primary School, our Early Reading curriculum is designed to place the needs and aspirations of our pupils at the heart of their learning journey. We deliver a knowledge-rich, ambitious, and inclusive curriculum that empowers every child to master the alphabetic code and develop a lifelong love of literature, helping them to "Be the BEST they can be." Our intent is underpinned by four key attitudes, ensuring pupils develop the character and resilience to thrive:
BELIEVE: Building Confidence and Belonging
We foster an environment where children believe in their potential by ensuring early success.
By matching books strictly to phonic knowledge, we build the confidence necessary for children to see themselves as readers.
We believe that the 'invisible privilege' of being read to must become a 'universal right' for every child at Hillside.
ENGAGE: Curiosity and Connection
We inspire curiosity through a diverse and ambitious reading spine.
In EYFS and Key Stage 1, we prioritise daily Storytime to bridge the 'cultural capital' gap, engaging children with complex narratives that motivate them to read independently.
SUCCEED: Precision and Mastery
Success is rooted in the mastery of the 44 speed sounds.
We aim for all pupils to meet or exceed national standards, moving from mechanical decoding to the automaticity required for deep comprehension.
TRY: Resilience and Hard Thinking
We cultivate resilience through 'hard thinking.' Whether tackling a new digraph or navigating a 'resistant text' during Storytime, pupils are encouraged to embrace challenges and learn from the process of decoding.

About Us
Greenshaw Learning Trust
Greenshaw Learning Trust
Hillside Primary School is an academy in the Greenshaw Learning Trust. Find out more about the Trust here.
The Greenshaw Learning Trust is an academy trust, a charitable company with the sole purpose of maintaining and developing academy schools, to provide comprehensive and inclusive education for the public benefit, funded by the Department for Education.
The Trust seeks to build a ‘family’ of like-minded schools that share essential values and a common ethos and vision for education and learning, and collaborate to provide mutual support, share their good practice and learn from each other.
Each school in the Trust will retain and develop its own distinct character, led by its own leadership team and local governing body. The Trust will provide the support and infrastructure the schools need to enable them to develop and improve and for the school leadership and governing body to achieve their objectives for their school.
Trust Policies can be found here

Learning Curriculum
Learning Curriculum
Our Subjects
Music
Music
At Hillside Primary School, our Music curriculum is designed to place the needs and aspirations of our pupils at the heart of their learning. Our bespoke curriculum is ambitious and inclusive which empowers every child to be a musician, fostering a deep love of music and performance to help them "Be the BEST they can be." Our Music curriculum intent is underpinned by four key attitudes for learning, which ensure our pupils develop the character and resilience needed to thrive in the modern world:
We deliver a high-quality Music curriculum that equips pupils with the Substantive Knowledge (musical elements and dimensions) and Disciplinary Knowledge (the skills of listening, singing, playing, improvising, composing, and performing) essential for achieving and exceeding the expected standard. Our curriculum is anchored by six ‘Big Ideas’ that build progressively. When pupils encounter a Big Idea, they revisit prior units to make connections, building the mental schema required to understand how music is constructed, enjoyed, and shared across different cultures and eras.
BELIEVE: Building Confidence and Belonging
Culture, Context & Style (Big Ideas): We foster an environment where children believe in their unique musical potential by exploring how diverse genres, from Classical and Jazz to Hip-Hop and Reggae, connect communities globally.
Vocabulary for success: We believe that vocabulary is the gateway to high achievement. Pupils move from simple language in EYFS to mastering tier-3 terminology such as 'Pulse', 'Pitch', 'Syncopation', 'Notation', and 'Texture'.
Inclusive Achievement: Through pre-teaching rhythms, visual scaffolding, and SEND adaptations (such as using adapted instruments or icon-based notation), we ensure all pupils - regardless of background - believe they can access Age Related Expectations (ARE) and beyond during practical music-making.
ENGAGE: Curiosity and Connection
Instrumentation & Sound (Big Idea): We spark curiosity by tracking how different instruments produce sound, exploring everything from standard classroom percussion and glockenspiels to electronic synthesizers and classical orchestral sections.
Musical Enquiry (Disciplinary): Pupils engage as active listeners. They move from moving their bodies to a basic pulse in Key Stage 1 to critically appraising a piece of music, identifying its structure, instrumentation, and emotional impact in Key Stage 2.
Local and Global Identity: Our curriculum draws heavily on connection. By engaging with both local musical traditions and a vast array of global styles within the Charanga framework, children see themselves within the curriculum and connect their own voices to the wider global musical story.
SUCCEED: Precision and Mastery
Pulse & Rhythm (Big Idea): Success is rooted in a precise internal rhythm. Pupils move from simple physical clapping games to accurately reading, keeping, and playing complex rhythmic patterns against a steady counter-pulse.
Composition & Notation (Disciplinary): Mastery is shown when pupils can move past simple experimentation to intentionally creating their own musical motifs, eventually recording them using graphic or standard formal notation.
Substantive Mastery: Pupils succeed when they can confidently manipulate the dimensions of music, intentionally altering pitch, dynamics, and tempo to achieve a specific expressive effect in performance.
TRY: Resilience and Hard Thinking
Improvisation & Performance (Big Ideas): Pupils embrace 'hard thinking' and vulnerability to stand up and perform or improvise phrases in front of peers, building massive personal resilience.
Critical Evaluation (Disciplinary): We cultivate a culture where children are not afraid to 'try' new ideas, evaluate their own musical compositions, accept constructive feedback, and adapt their work to improve the final group performance.
Melody & Texture (Big Ideas): Children develop resilience by studying how complex layers of sound fit together, moving from simple unison singing to complex rounds, solo parts, and instrumental harmonies.
Through this vocabulary-rich, sequential curriculum, Hillside pupils do not just 'learn' music; they think and act like musicians, building the character and cultural capital needed to thrive in the modern world.

Learning Curriculum
Learning Curriculum
Our Subjects
Reading
At Hillside Primary School, our Reading curriculum is designed to place the needs and aspirations of our pupils at the heart of their learning. Our bespoke curriculum is ambitious and inclusive, empowering every child to be a fluent, critical, and lifelong reader, fostering a deep understanding of literature to help them "Be the BEST they can be". Our Reading curriculum intent is underpinned by four key attitudes for learning, ensuring our pupils develop the character and literacy skills needed to thrive in the modern world:
We deliver a high-quality Reading curriculum that equips pupils with Word Reading (decoding and fluency) and Comprehension (linguistic knowledge and inference) essential for achieving and exceeding the expected standard. Our curriculum is anchored by 'Big Ideas' that build progressively. When pupils encounter these concepts, they revisit prior learning to build the mental schema required to navigate complex texts.
BELIEVE: Building Confidence and Belonging
Word Reading & Fluency (Big Idea): We foster an environment where children believe in their potential by mastering the mechanics of reading. From hearing initial sounds in EYFS to applying complex etymology and morphology in Year 6, we build the confidence to decode any text.
Vocabulary for Success: We believe vocabulary is the gateway to high achievement. Pupils move from discussing simple word meanings in Year 2 to explaining complex vocabulary in context and using dictionaries independently by Year 4.
Inclusive Achievement: Through rigorous phonics (GPCs) and scaffolded support, we ensure all pupils – regardless of background – believe they can access Age-Related Expectations (ARE) and beyond.
ENGAGE: Curiosity and Connection
Reading for Pleasure (Big Idea): We spark curiosity by exposing children to a wide range of contemporary and classic poetry, stories, and non-fiction texts.
Enquiry & Discussion: Pupils engage as active participants. They move from taking turns in discussions in Year 1 to building on others' ideas and challenging views courteously in Upper Key Stage 2.
Retelling & Performance: Pupils connect with texts by retelling myths and legends and preparing poems or plays for performance, using intonation and volume to engage an audience.
SUCCEED: Precision and Mastery
Retrieval & Sequence (Big Idea): Success is rooted in precision. Pupils move from identifying titles and events in Year 1 to retrieving information from fiction and non-fiction texts across multiple sentences to link meaning by Year 5.
Summarising & Themes: Mastery is shown when pupils can move beyond simple sequencing to identify main ideas across multiple paragraphs and discuss recurring themes across a wide range of writing.
Substantive Mastery: Pupils succeed when they can distinguish between fact and opinion and provide reasoned justifications for their views by the end of Year 6.
TRY: Resilience and Hard Thinking
Inference & Evidence (Big Idea): Pupils embrace 'hard thinking' by moving beyond literal meaning. They 'try' different interpretations, using a Point Evidence Explain structure in Year 5 and 6 to justify inferences about characters' motives.
Prediction & Analysis: We cultivate a culture where children are not afraid to make complex predictions. Pupils transition from predicting based on what has been read to making implied predictions based on themes, conventions, and knowledge of the author.
Authorial Intent: Children develop resilience by evaluating how authors use figurative language and identifying how structure and presentation contribute to the overall meaning of a text.

Learning Curriculum
Learning Curriculum
Our Subjects
Science
At Hillside Primary School, our Science curriculum is designed to place the needs and aspirations of our pupils at the heart of their learning. Our bespoke curriculum is ambitious and inclusive, empowering every child to be a scientist and fostering a deep curiosity about the natural world to help them "Be the BEST they can be." Our Science curriculum intent is underpinned by four key attitudes for learning, which ensure our pupils develop the character and resilience needed to thrive in a scientific and technological world:
We deliver a high-quality Science curriculum that equips pupils with the Substantive Knowledge (the 'Big Ideas' of Biology, Chemistry, and Physics) and Disciplinary Knowledge (the 'Working Scientifically' skills) essential for achieving and exceeding the expected standard. Our 'Big Ideas' link learning across all year groups. By revisiting these themes, pupils build on what they already know – moving from simple hands-on activities to a deeper understanding of scientific concepts.
BELIEVE: Building Confidence and Belonging
Biology and The Self (Big Idea): We foster an environment where children believe in their unique potential by exploring their own body. From identifying body parts in EYFS to mastering the complexities of the circulatory system in Year 6, pupils develop a sense of identity and an understanding of how to keep their bodies healthy.
Vocabulary for Success: We believe that vocabulary is the key to high achievement. Pupils move from simple language in EYFS to mastering tier-3 terminology such as 'Germination', 'Solubility', 'Photosynthesis', and 'Refraction'.
Inclusive Achievement: Through pre-teaching, scaffolding, and SEND adaptations, we ensure all pupils – regardless of background – believe they can access Age Related Expectations (ARE) and beyond.
ENGAGE: Curiosity and Connection
Physics and The Natural World (Big Idea): We spark curiosity by tracking how the physical world works. Investigating how sounds are produced by vibrations or exploring the movement of the Earth and Moon, pupils engage with the 'how' and 'why' of their environment.
Scientific Enquiry (Disciplinary): Pupils engage as active researchers. They move from asking simple 'Yes/No' questions in Key Stage 1 to independently identifying variables and using secondary sources to research unfamiliar concepts in Key Stage 2.
Local Identity: Our curriculum draws on our locality. By studying local animals and how they are adapted to the Gloucester environment, children see themselves within the curriculum and connect their school to the wider natural world.
SUCCEED: Precision and Mastery
Chemistry and States of Matter (Big Idea): Success is rooted in observation. Pupils move from simple sorting of materials in EYFS to mastering an understanding of solids, liquids, and gases, and the mechanics of the water cycle.
Observing and Measuring (Disciplinary): Mastery is shown when pupils can move from non-standard measures to taking measurements with increasing accuracy and precision, using scientific equipment.
Substantive Mastery: Pupils succeed when they can explain the 'causal relationships' in science – such as how the number and voltage of cells in a circuit influence the brightness of a bulb.
TRY: Resilience and Hard Thinking
Evolution and Inheritance (Big Idea): Pupils embrace 'hard thinking' to understand complex concepts such as how living things have changed over millions of years and how offspring inherit characteristics while remaining unique.
Evidence and Argument (Disciplinary): We cultivate a culture where children are not afraid to 'try' new hypotheses. In Key Stage 2, pupils use evidence to challenge statements and evaluate the 'degree of trust' they have in their own results, understanding that scientific ideas are refined through trial and error.
Resilience in Testing: Children develop resilience by setting up fair tests, identifying irregularities, and being prepared to change their opinions based on data.
Through this vocabulary-rich, sequential curriculum, Hillside pupils do not just 'learn' science; they think like scientists, building the character and cultural capital needed to thrive in the modern world.

Learning Curriculum
Learning Curriculum
Curriculum Overview
Curriculum Overview
Curriculum
Our curriculum intent is, “To provide pupils with exciting, challenging and engaging learning opportunities that give a lifelong passion for learning and provide them with the skills and knowledge to pursue their interests and passions.”
We follow a curriculum that develops our children in an engaging way encouraging high expectation. Our curriculum is purposefully broad and children have opportunities to participate in a wide range of cross-curricular activities as well as in music, performance and sport.
We encourage children to question and to think both logically and creatively. We aim to make the children as independent as possible and encourage them to find their own solutions to problems or tasks they have been set, beginning the journey to becoming lifelong learners.
Our curriculum promotes resilience and encourages children to reflect on their learning and how they learn in a systematic way. The curriculum includes all that the children are taught and experience. This is not only the formal requirements of the National Curriculum but also our extra-curricular activities such as: after school and lunchtime clubs which enrich children’s learning and offer opportunities beyond that of the national curriculum; visitors to school during assemblies and other special occasions, some of whom are from our local community; school trips related to curriculum area that children are learning about; sporting events both competitive and experiential to learn new sports etc. We believe that these additional activities enrich the educational experience of our children.
Our curriculum also aims to help children form positive relationships with adults and children in order to learn how to work collaboratively in preparation for becoming responsible members of our local community both in the present and in their future adult lives.
Here you can find information on the school curriculum with any additional specific information available on the individual Class pages.
Reading and Phonics
We believe that a quality English curriculum should develop children’s love of reading, writing and discussion. We aim to inspire an appreciation of our rich and varied literary heritage and a habit of reading widely and often. We recognise the importance of nurturing a culture where children take pride in their writing, can write clearly and accurately and adapt their language and style for a range of contexts. We want to inspire children to be confident in the art of speaking and listening and who can use discussion to communicate and further their learning.
We believe that children need to develop a secure knowledge-base in English, which follows a clear pathway of progression as they advance through the primary curriculum. Books have been selected to have an approach where books are cumulative through theme and progressive by complexity of text. We believe that a secure basis in English skills is crucial to a high quality education and will give our children the tools they need to participate fully as a member of society.
Reading is taught using a whole class approach. High quality texts are chosen and children use the VIPERS to identify the 6 reading domains within the National Curriculum. These are the key areas which children need to understand in order to improve their comprehension of texts.
Phonics
Phonics is a way of teaching children to read quickly and skillfully. Children are taught how to: recognise the sounds that each individual letter makes; identify the sounds that different combinations of letters make; and blend these sounds together from left to right to make a word.

Through the Read, Write Inc. Programme, children learn the alphabetic code: the 150+ graphemes that represent the 44 speech sounds. They rapidly learn sounds and the letter, or groups of letters, they need to represent them.
What is Read, Write Inc. (RWI) phonics?
The RWI phonics programme is a systematic and synthetic way of teaching children to read. It was developed by Ruth Miskin, more information can be found at www.ruthmiskinliteracy.com
Children will begin the programme in Reception and will remain on the programme until they are reading at an expected Year 2 level. Our aim is for most children to have finished by the end of Year 2, however some children will continue RWI intervention if needed.
The children will have a daily RWI phonics lesson, which includes reading and writing activities. A few children who may need extra support to maintain progress will work with an adult for an extra 10 minutes a day.
How do we know RWI works?
Schools embedding this programme have been recognised by OFSTED in the HMI ‘Reading by Six Report’ (November 2010) as an example of how the best schools teach reading.

Mathematics
Mathematics is an important creative discipline that helps us to understand and change the World. We want all pupils to experience the beauty, power and enjoyment of mathematics and develop a sense of curiosity about the subject.
We foster positive ‘can do’ attitudes and believe all children can achieve in mathematics. We teach for secure and deep understanding of mathematical concepts. We use mistakes as an essential part of learning and provide challenge through rich and sophisticated problems before acceleration through new content.
Outdoor Learning
The best classroom has no ceiling.
The outdoor learning environment is a rich, dynamic, natural space that is ever changing and a perfect environment for learning and development in children (and adults) of all ages. Its value as an essential learning resource has been recognised by many pieces of research and more recently within the EYFS, particularly within the principle of 'Enabling Environments'.
